source_evidence: Lecturer also says F_X(x)=P(X<x); the book preserves rather than repairs this convention.
mathematical_analysis: P(X<x) is the left-limit version, not the usual right-continuous CDF at atoms. For X=0 a.s., P(X<0)=0 whereas the standard F(0)=1.
recommended_disposition: Use P(X<=x), or explicitly name and distinguish the left-continuous version.

source_evidence: Source says the sample is selected completely at random and then calls X_1,...,X_n iid; it supplies no sampling-design assumption that entails independence.
mathematical_analysis: Random sampling without replacement is dependent. Iid requires an explicit model, e.g. independent draws/with-replacement or a superpopulation assumption.
recommended_disposition: State iid sampling as a modelling assumption; do not infer it solely from randomness/representativeness.

source_evidence: Source restricts its exposition to a density and calls likelihood the joint density; it does not state a parameter space, attainment condition, positive-likelihood domain, or boundary qualification for scores.
mathematical_analysis: Likelihood is a function of theta for fixed data, formed from pmf/density, not a CDF. A score equation finds only interior candidates and log L needs L>0.
recommended_disposition: Define L(theta;x) over explicit Theta, qualify score equations as interior candidates, and use pmf/density rather than distribution function.

source_evidence: Source board makes the same max-only indicator reduction; no lower-support condition is retained.
mathematical_analysis: The product is zero if any observed x_j<=0, even when x*=max_j x_j lies in (0,theta]. Correctly it includes 1_{min_j x_j>0} as a theta-constant data-support factor.
recommended_disposition: Retain the lower-support factor, then say it may be suppressed conditional on data in (0,infinity)^n.

source_evidence: Source/board gives the stationary equations and two displayed estimators but neither states sigma^2>0 nor handles n=1/all-equal data.
mathematical_analysis: If residual sum of squares is zero, likelihood diverges as sigma^2 downarrow 0; the candidate variance 0 is outside the normal family and no MLE is attained.
recommended_disposition: State mu in R and sigma^2>0; qualify the result to positive residual sum of squares and explain nonexistence otherwise.

source_evidence: Source does explain a one-to-one inverse moment map and supplies U(-theta,theta) as a failure case, but does not state finite absolute moments; book's general assertion is still unqualified.
mathematical_analysis: Strong-law convergence of the jth sample moment needs iid sampling and E|X|^j<infinity; a moment system can lack a unique in-parameter-space solution.
recommended_disposition: State integrability and iid hypotheses plus existence/uniqueness (or a defined measurable selection) in Theta.

source_evidence: The lecture globally fixes X_1,...,X_n as iid at lines 13-17 and source expressly uses iid Y_j in the proof. Earlier moment indexing uses j>=1, conventionally an integer index.
mathematical_analysis: A standalone theorem could restate iid and say positive integer k, but in the established lecture setup these are inherited conventions/hypotheses. This is not a material mathematical failure of the proposition as presented.
recommended_disposition: No required correction; optionally restate 'positive integer' and iid for local self-containment.

source_evidence: The Cramer--Rao supplement is book-added; transcript proceeds from MoM examples directly to estimator properties.
mathematical_analysis: 'Sufficient smoothness' does not justify the scalar Cramer--Rao form. Moving support U(0,theta) supplies a counterexample: 2X is unbiased with variance theta^2/3 while naive score information gives theta^2 lower bound.
recommended_disposition: State precise regularity, scalar-parameter, and unbiasedness assumptions; warn that moving-support U(0,theta) is nonregular.

source_evidence: Source writes the same formula for a generic epsilon without limiting 0<epsilon<theta; no case split is given.
mathematical_analysis: For epsilon>=theta, P(X*<theta-epsilon)=0, while ((theta-epsilon)/theta)^n is not generally zero or even nonnegative. Also use X*<=theta a.s. to connect this event to absolute error.
recommended_disposition: Split 0<epsilon<theta from epsilon>=theta, then state the absolute-error equivalence.

source_evidence: Source gives the same Bessel correction without an n>=2 restriction.
mathematical_analysis: S^2 uses denominator n-1 and is undefined for n=1.
recommended_disposition: State n>=2 before defining S^2 and cross-reference the normal-MLE boundary case.
